model_title: Gland Packing (Stuffing Box) Assembly with Lantern Ring & Flush

introduction.definition: A gland packing assembly seals a pump shaft with rings of braided packing compressed in a stuffing box by a gland follower. The packing presses on the shaft sleeve and throttles leakage; a small controlled leakage lubricates and cools it. A lantern ring in the middle of the set can feed clean flush water.
applications: Water, slurry and general service pumps
Valve stems, agitators and older plant equipment

pressure.title: Pressure is broken down along the packing
pressure.description: Packing seals by throttling: the gland compresses the rings so they press radially on the sleeve, and leakage flows along a long, narrow path, losing pressure ring by ring. Most of the pressure drop happens in the rings nearest the gland, so those wear first. A packed gland must leak a little (≈ 40–60 drops per minute) — the liquid lubricates and removes friction heat; over-tightening burns the packing and grooves the sleeve. The lantern ring feeds clean flush liquid into the middle of the set.

The gland follower compresses them.
Pressure drops ring by ring along the shaft.
The lantern ring distributes flush liquid.
A small leakage lubricates and cools.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Gland Packing Assembly.
Check leakage rate and gland temperature.
Adjust gland nuts evenly by small steps.
Repack; inspect sleeve; replace if grooved.
Watch for burnt packing: smoke, no leakage, hot gland. Common cause: over-tightening, no flush.
Watch for excess leakage: steady stream. Common cause: worn packing / sleeve, shaft runout.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
